title: 1 Kings 7
paragraphs: ¹ Solomon also built his own palace, which took him thirteen years to complete. ² He built the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon — a hundred cubits long, fifty wide, and thirty high — supported by four rows of cedar columns with cedar beams across the tops. ³ The ceiling above the beams rested on forty-five pillars, fifteen per row, and was covered with cedar. ⁴ There were three rows of windows facing each other in sets of three, ⁵ and all the doors and doorframes were square — again, windows facing windows in three tiers.

⁶ He built a colonnade fifty cubits long and thirty wide, with a covered porch in front supported by pillars and a canopy overhead. ⁷ He also built the throne room — the Hall of Justice, where he would hear cases — and he paneled it with cedar from floor to ceiling. ⁸ His own living quarters, behind the hall in the inner courtyard, were built the same way. He also built a palace for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married, just like this hall. ⁹ All these buildings, from foundation to roofline and from the outside to the great courtyard, were built of fine dressed stone cut to measure and sawed smooth on all sides. ¹⁰ The foundations were laid with great stones — slabs of eight and ten cubits.

¹¹ Above the foundation were more dressed stones cut to size, and cedar beams. ¹² The great outer courtyard had three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams all the way around, just like the inner courtyard of the LORD's house and the entrance hall of the palace. ¹³ King Solomon sent to Tyre and brought a man named Hiram. ¹⁴ He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a craftsman from Tyre who worked in bronze. Hiram was brilliant — a master of all kinds of bronze work — and he came to King Solomon and carried out all the bronze work assigned to him. ¹⁵ He cast two bronze pillars, each eighteen cubits tall and twelve cubits in circumference.

¹⁶ He also made two capitals of cast bronze to set on top of the pillars, each one five cubits tall. ¹⁷ He decorated the capitals with lattice netting and twisted chains — seven strands of chainwork for each capital. ¹⁸ He made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates running around each network to cover the capitals at the top, and he did the same for both capitals. ¹⁹ The capitals on top of the pillars in the porch were shaped like lilies, four cubits tall. ²⁰ Above the rounded part beside the network, pomegranates ran in rows all the way around — two hundred pomegranates encircling each capital.

²¹ He erected the pillars at the porch of the temple. The right pillar he named Jachin, and the left pillar he named Boaz. ²² The tops of both pillars were shaped like lilies. And so the work on the pillars was finished. ²³ He made the great bronze basin — the Sea — ten cubits across, perfectly round, five cubits deep, and thirty cubits in circumference. ²⁴ All around the rim, just below the brim, were two rows of gourds encircling it — ten gourds per cubit, cast as part of the basin. ²⁵ The Sea rested on twelve bronze oxen — three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east — with the Sea mounted on top of them and all their haunches turned inward.

²⁶ The basin was a handsbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like a cup — like the petals of a lily. It held two thousand baths. ²⁷ Hiram also made ten bronze stands, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits tall. ²⁸ The stands were built with side panels set in frames, ²⁹ and on those panels — between the rails — were carved lions, oxen, and cherubim. Above and below the lions and oxen were decorative wreaths of hammered work. ³⁰ Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles. At the four corners were supports cast as part of the stand, and the supports beneath the basin were also cast with decorative wreaths at each side.

³¹ The opening at the top of each stand — inside the capital — was a cubit deep. The opening itself was round, a cubit and a half across, and around its edges were carvings and panels — square, not round. ³² Below the opening were four wheels fitted with bronze axles connected to the body of the stand. Each wheel was a cubit and a half in diameter. ³³ The wheels were crafted like chariot wheels — their axles, hubs, spokes, and rims all cast in bronze. ³⁴ Each of the four corners had a cast support that was part of the stand itself. ³⁵ At the top of each stand was a round collar half a cubit high, and the panels and frames at the top were cast as part of the stand.

³⁶ On the surfaces of the panels and frames he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees, with decorative borders all around. ³⁷ This is how he made all ten stands — all poured from the same mold, the same size, the same design. ³⁸ He also made ten bronze basins, one for each stand. Each basin was four cubits across and held forty baths. ³⁹ He placed five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, and he set the Sea on the southeast corner. ⁴⁰ Hiram finished the basins, the shovels, and the bowls. With that, all the bronze work he had been doing for King Solomon on the LORD's house was complete.

⁴¹ This is what he made: the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of lattice netting to cover the two bowls; ⁴² four hundred pomegranates for the two lattice nets — two rows of pomegranates for each net covering the bowl-shaped capitals; ⁴³ the ten stands with their ten basins; ⁴⁴ the one great Sea with the twelve oxen beneath it; ⁴⁵ and the pots, shovels, and bowls. All these objects that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of burnished bronze.

⁴⁶ The king had them cast in the clay ground of the Jordan Valley, between Succoth and Zarethan. ⁴⁷ Solomon did not have all these vessels weighed, because there were so many — the total weight of the bronze was never determined. ⁴⁸ Solomon also made all the furnishings that belonged inside the LORD's house: the golden altar; the golden table for the bread of the Presence; ⁴⁹ the pure gold lampstands — five on the right and five on the left, in front of the inner sanctuary — with their gold flowers, lamps, and tongs; ⁵⁰ the gold bowls, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, incense dishes, and censers; and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner sanctuary and for the doors of the main hall of the temple.

⁵¹ When all the work King Solomon had done for the house of the LORD was finished, he brought in the silver and gold and all the sacred objects that his father David had dedicated, and placed them in the treasuries of the LORD's house.
